transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (CTO, Stratos), Aisha Khan (DevOps), Liam O'Neil (SRE)

Summary: Quick discovery on reliability/incident tolerance and how Redwood handles fallbacks, multi-region routing, and SLA commitments.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, with priya our s-e, can you do quick intros?
00:10 Jordan Miles: yeah i'm jordan, cto at stratos, primarily focused on infra and uptime, we've been evaluating hosted vs dedicated for our LLM endpoints, big concerns around incident tolerance and regional outages.
00:25 Aisha Khan: hi i'm aisha, devops, i'm worried about data residency and failover planning, we run most of our traffic out of us-east and eu-west.
00:36 Priya Patel: great, thanks. quick note, i'll ask some perf questions and propose a bench plan.
00:45 Liam O'Neil: liam here, s-r-e, we own oncall, so we need predictable SLOs and clear fallback behavior.
00:53 Alex Chen: perfect. jordan, what's your current stack and how do you handle model serving today?
01:05 Jordan Miles: today it's mostly in-house, some endpoints on gcp runnning vertex, but cost and ops are killing us. we want to push more to hosted if reliability and compliance check out.
01:20 Alex Chen: makes sense. what are your target SLOs and what constitutes failure for you?
01:30 Jordan Miles: we want 99.95 p99 latency under 300ms for short prompts, and 99.9 uptime monthly. failure modes: region outage, GPU OOMs during spikes, model regressions.
01:45 Priya Patel: helpful. two quick architecture levers we typically recommend: multi-region routing with health-based failover, and tiered fallback policies — e.g. same-model on a different region, then a smaller quantized variant, then cached prefix or canned response.
02:05 Aisha Khan: can you do auto-failover across clouds? like if aws eu-west is down can it route to gcp?
02:15 Priya Patel: yes, we support cross-region and cross-cloud routing policies. we do DNS and smart routing in the control plane; you can set policy by latency, cost, or region. during failover we also surface metrics and trace links in the console. slight note: cold-starts on a different region can add latency — we mitigate with standby warm pools or reserved capacity (dedicated).
02:45 Liam O'Neil: what's the typical RTO when switching regions?
02:50 Priya Patel: depends on your warm pool. with hosted on shared capacity it's usually a few 10s of seconds to a couple minutes if we need to spin up a variant. with Dedicated reserved GPUs you can get sub-10s cutover because of pre-warmed nodes.
03:10 Jordan Miles: curious about fallback to smaller models — do you guarantee the semantics? we need to avoid hallucination regressions.
03:22 Priya Patel: good question. we don't change model responses transparently; fallbacks are a policy you configure. recommended pattern: first fallback path is same model but different region or capacity tier; second is a quantized/optimized variant pinned to a validation set — we run regression checks during rollout and you can set quality gates. last resort is prefix cache or canned response which is deterministic.
03:48 Aisha Khan: do you keep audit logs for these switches? we need full traceability for compliance.
03:55 Alex Chen: yes, audit logs and route change events are logged, also SSO and role-based access. we can ship KMS integration for key control.
04:08 Liam O'Neil: SLA wise, you said 99.9 vs 99.95 depending on tier? what's in the enterprise SLA?
04:15 Alex Chen: hosted has standard SLA tiers — the hosted public offering usually targets 99.9 for most customers; Dedicated backed by reserved capacity gets higher targets and an SLA addendum — for example 99.95 with financial credits in the contract. final numbers depend on committed capacity and regions. we'll include exact SLA text in the deck.
04:38 Jordan Miles: what's your incident escalation like? we need clear runbook integration and oncall paging.
04:45 Priya Patel: we offer alert hooks, webhook integrations, and you can forward traces into your pager system. for Dedicated and Private we do a higher-touch SLA with 24/7 support options and a named escalation path.
04:58 Aisha Khan: wanted to flag data residency — in some regions we can't route out of country. can we pin certain customers to a region and only fail within that boundary?
05:08 Priya Patel: yes, you can restrict failover boundaries. e.g., EU-only fallback to other EU regions, and for Private deployments you can fully control the private control plane so nothing leaves your VPC.
05:22 Liam O'Neil: any gotchas on KV cache or prefix caching when failing over? does cache miss rate spike?
05:30 Priya Patel: yes, cache misses can spike on cold-regions; our approach is warm-KV replication for critical prefixes or active replication options. if you rely heavily on cache for latency, Dedicated helps because replication windows are tighter; otherwise expect a brief cold penalty while caches refill.
05:52 Jordan Miles: ok, sounds like a tradeoff: hosted faster to get started but dedicated gives more predictable cutover and better SLAs.
06:00 Alex Chen: exactly. for many customers we start with hosted + canary routing and then move to Dedicated for production after we learn traffic patterns.
06:12 Aisha Khan: question on testing: can we run a simulated region failover test?
06:18 Priya Patel: yes, we do chaos-style drills in staging; we'll provision a test plan that tears down a region and measures RTO/RPO, and we capture traces and the console shows fallbacks. we'll propose a runbook and run it with your SREs.
06:35 Liam O'Neil: perfect. also want to measure error-mode behaviors: what happens to inflight requests during fallback?
06:42 Priya Patel: inflight tokens may be retried according to your request policy, we can configure idempotency keys and retry windows; we also surface partial responses and have deterministic fallback for streaming. there can be token duplication in edge cases so we recommend idempotent request IDs for stateful workflows.
07:05 Jordan Miles: any enterprise customers using cross-cloud multi-region with you?
07:10 Alex Chen: yes, a couple finserv and ecom customers run hybrid with aws + gcp + private on-prem pools, they use smart routing and we help tune burst capacity.
07:22 Jordan Miles: okay next, pricing: does Dedicated require a long commit?
07:28 Alex Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity monthly or annual commits; we can do a pilot month for evaluation. pricing varies by GPU class and region. we'll send the pricing sheet.
07:38 Aisha Khan: and security pack?
07:40 Alex Chen: we'll share SOC2, ISO, KMS integration docs and an architecture diagram for Private.
07:46 Priya Patel: action items: we'll run a baseline benchmark between your staging endpoints and our hosted endpoints including cross-region failover simulation. i'll propose dates.
07:55 Jordan Miles: sounds good. any questions from you all?
08:00 Liam O'Neil: how do you handle model rollbacks if a model regression causes high error rates?
08:08 Priya Patel: we have version pinning and automated rollbacks tied to eval sets and health checks; you can set automatic revert-to-last-known-good and notify ops.
08:20 Jordan Miles: great. let's recap.
08:24 Alex Chen: recap: Priya will propose benchmark dates and run a failover sim; Alex will send Dedicated pricing and SLA deck and security pack; Jordan to provide IPs and preferred regions. we'll aim to reconvene after the benchmark.
08:40 Jordan Miles: thanks, talk soon.
08:44 Alex Chen: thanks everyone, bye.

Notes: transcription has occasional name misspellings and filler words; timestamps approximate. Links shared during call: pricing deck (link), security pack (Box link), benchmarking spreadsheet (internal link).

End of transcript.
